declaration.name: Declaration
declaration.message:
I, the applicant, confirm that the information that is contained in this application is true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief and that I have made appropriate enquiries to ensure the accuracy of the information that I have submitted. For the avoidance of doubt, I further confirm: -

1) That I understand that if, in completing this form, I provide information that I know or suspect to be false then I will be committing a criminal offence for which I may be liable for criminal prosecution.

2) I have permission from all vessel owners to apply for a fishing vessel licence for the vessel named in this application.

3) The vessel named in this application, is registered to the vessel owners under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.

4) Vessel owners commit to complying with all conditions attached to the licence.

5) All vessel owners understand that if any of the details provided in this application change, any licence issued will be invalid.

6) All vessel owners confirm to the best of their knowledge the vessel has never received a decommissioning grant in the UK or any EC member state.

7) Vessel owners hold the licence entitlements listed in this application

8) All vessel owners understand that this application is for a domestic licence only. An external waters licence will need to be applied for separately from the UK SIA team uksia@marinemanagement.org.uk

Please note, after you submit this form a confirmation page will appear with a reference number and instructions on your next steps for submitting relevant documentation to support your application.

step_1.name: Are you applying to license an English or Crown Dependency vessel

metadata.guidance_markdown:
## You can apply once you have:

1) the certificate of registry in your name(s) from one of the following;

* Maritime & Coastguard Agency (MCA) UK Ship Register
* Isle of Man Ship Registry
* Jersey ships Registry
* Registry of British ships from Guernsey Harbours.

2) at least one fishing entitlement in your name to license your vessel

3) an English, Isle of Man, Jersey or Guernsey port, letter, number (PLN) on your vessel. 

## The application form must be filled in by:

* the registered owner(s) of the vessel to be licensed
* an authorised signatory for the registered owner(s)
* a person with power of attorney for the registered owner(s)

## To complete this application, you will need to have available:

* the certificate of registry
* vessel owner(s) contact details
* nominee and/or nominated person contact details
* the details for the entitlements you want to use to license this vessel (found on your AFL7 section D or AFL19 section F). The holder's details on the entitlements must be the same as the vessel owner details on the certificate of registry

If you are applying on behalf of a company based in Jersey, Guernsey or the Isle of Man, we will need the certificate of registration and the list of company directors.

Please make sure the entitlement(s) you want to use to license this vessel are suitable for your requirements:

* overall length of the vessel (over 10 metres, or 10 metres and under)
* licence category
* licence permits – shellfish (all vessel lengths), scallop and beam trawl areas 4 and 7 (over 10m vessels only)
* engine power
* tonnage

Eligibility to fish for bass using regulated gears does not transfer ownership with a licence entitlement. The authority remains with the vessel. If you are replacing a vessel that has a bass authorisation, a transfer of authorisation will be considered but is subject to strict rules.

If MMO has given permission for the bass authorisation to be retained to be placed on another vessel in your ownership you will be asked to upload the confirmation letter or email during this application.

For vessels over 10m in overall length, in order to carry and use regulated gears in the Sole Recovery Zone (SRZ) and area 7d, referred to as Cod Area 7d, a vessel must have eligibility through a known track record or via the transfer of a single licence (or the aggregation of two or more licence entitlements) where the originating vessel(s) has such a record of fishing activity with selective gears in these areas.


## Important
If the entitlements do not contain enough engine power or tonnage to license this vessel, you will need to obtain another entitlement to cover the shortfall. 

If the engine power and tonnage on the entitlement are greater than the vessel requirements, any excess will be lost forever unless you first submit an AFL19 application to separate a fishing vessel licence entitlement. This is also known as disaggregating an entitlement.

Before you proceed with an application to separate a fishing vessel licence entitlement, please ensure that by disaggregating an entitlement it won’t affect the resulting shellfish, scallop or beam trawl permit. [To access an AFL19 application form select this link](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/fishing-vessel-licensing-forms))

step_2.name: What licence category do you wish to apply for

metadata.guidance_markdown:
## Licence category you are applying for.

### Over 10 metre vessels
Please select the category of licence you are applying for from the list below. For more information on the licence categories please select this link [fishing vessel licence categories](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/fishing-vessel-licence-types).

### Vessels 10 metres and under
Category A is the single category for 10 metre and under licences. As of 01 January 2025, the licence cap on 10 metre and under vessels has been permanently removed.
metadata.hint_text: This will be shown on the licence entitlement - AFL7 section D or AFL19 section F.  The first category is for licence entitlements originating from vessels 10 metres and under, the remaining categories are for licence entitlements originating from vessels over 10 metres.

step_4.name: What is the official registration number

metadata.guidance_markdown:
For English and Guernsey registered vessels this can be found on the vessel's certificate of registry. It's shown as one letter, either A, B or C for an English vessel or G for a Guernsey vessel, followed by 5 numbers. 

If you are completing the form for an Isle of Man registered vessel, the registration number may be shown as either an M followed by three to four digits, or six digits on their own.

A Jersey registered vessel doesn't have an official number. To move on to the next question enter the PLN.

step_12.name: What are the main gears to be displayed on your fishing vessel licence

metadata.guidance_markdown:
Up to four gear types will be displayed on your licence for information only. This will not prevent you using other gear types not named on your licence, subject to the licence conditions for your licence category. 

If the pattern of your fishing permanently changes so that the type of gear stated in your licence no longer accurately reflects the vessel's activities, you should apply to update your licence so a new licence containing the correct information can be issued.

## Owner details

In this section, we will ask you questions about the name and contact details for the vessel owner(s). This may be a company, partnership or individual. If you are applying on behalf of a company we will ask you for the company registration number.

## Important

The vessel owner details must match the owner names on both the licence entitlement(s) and the certificate of registry for the vessel you are licensing.

If you have a court order authorising a licence to be issued to you, we will ask you to provide us with a copy of the court order once you have submitted this application.

step_54.name: Do you want to provide details for a nominee

metadata.guidance_markdown:
You can nominate a person other than the first vessel owner to receive all licences, notices and variations on your behalf. 

If you are nominating a person other than the first vessel owner to be the nominee, you will need to provide the following information;

* A named nominee for the licence and their contact details. This person will receive all licences, notices and variations. 

You will also have the opportunity to nominate a second person to receive licence variation notifications alongside the nominee.

metadata.page_heading: Bass, Cod Area 7d, and Sole Recovery Zone
metadata.guidance_markdown:
### For vessels of any length

1 . Does the vessel have a bass authorisation or has MMO given permission for a retained bass authorisation to be placed on a vessel in your ownership? You will be asked to upload the confirmation letter or email in the next step.

For more information visit [Bass Fishing Guidance - GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/bass-industry-guidance-2025/bass-fishing-guidance-2025#vessel-replacement-and-transfer-of-authorisation)

### For over 10m vessels only

1 . Does the vessel have Cod 7d eligibility or are you are using a licence entitlement with Cod 7d eligibility to license the vessel?  All entitlements that include engine power used to licence the vessel must have Cod 7d eligibility.

For more information visit [Rules on Cod in ICES area VIId - GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/manage-your-fishing-effort-cod-in-ices-area-viid/rules-on-cod-in-ices-area-viid)

2 . Does the vessel have Sole Recovery Zone eligibility or are you using a licence entitlement with SRZ eligibility to license the vessel?  All entitlements that include engine power used to licence the vessel must have SRZ eligibility.

For more information visit [Sole Recovery Zone rules - GOV.UK](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/manage-your-fishing-effort-sole-recovery-zone/sole-recovery-zone-rules)

step_93.name: Are you already registered on the Fish Hub Electronic Reporting System

metadata.guidance_markdown:
The FishHub Electronic Reporting System (ERS) is an online portal.

It can be used to view vessel data and submit sales notes of first-sale fish if you are a registered buyer or seller.

'First-sale fish' refers to fish from a United Kingdom fishing vessel which is offered for sale for the first time. This includes undersize fish.

step_93.prompt: Are you already registered on the Fish Hub Electronic Reporting System?

step_94.name: Do you want to register on the FishHub Electronic Reporting System

metadata.guidance_markdown:
By selecting yes, indicating you want to view vessel data, you will be set up as a Vessel Administrator.

A Vessel Administrator can see the vessel’s logbooks, sales notes and data.

An Administrator has the ability to add delegated persons to view the logbooks, create landing declarations and also if required to view any relevant sales notes for your vessel.

Please note this question does not relate to setting up on the Catch Recording system. You will receive a separate email invitation for Catch Recording.
